brief.outcome: Raise the share of started checkouts that are completed from about 28% to 40% by the end of January 2027, on a Shopify clothing store selling in India, without cutting margin.

ambition.goal_beyond: More of the shoppers who get as far as paying actually pay, and the store notices early when that slips again
rungs: Fix the abandoned-cart email that goes out today
Find where in checkout the other 72% leave (cost, payment, mobile, email) and fix the biggest causes
Keep checkout completion healthy: a weekly check by device and payment method that flags a drop before it costs a month
ambition.judge: Shopify's checkout-completion figure and completed orders, mobile and desktop, for the same number of weeks before and after; Klaviyo's placed-order revenue for the flow against a held-back group; the payment gateway's own failed-attempt report

brief.deliverable: A diagnosed and fixed checkout and abandoned-cart flow: the chosen store and email changes applied with the owner's approval, with a read-back of the result
done: Checkout completion figure checked against orders, or its limits stated
Every cause (payment failures, shipping cost, mobile, email) marked supported, refuted or unknown, with evidence
Owner picks the fixes, with reasons recorded
New abandoned-cart and checkout emails drafted in Klaviyo and the store changes prepared
Changes applied only with the owner's yes to each one, each registered as a test first
Results read against the registered metric and guardrails, with learnings saved
guardrails: Margin per order does not fall: no new discounts or cuts to price
Add-to-cart rate (about 9% today) does not fall
Returns and cancellations do not rise
Email unsubscribes and spam complaints do not rise
limits: The Rs 999 free-shipping threshold stays as it is
Shopify is read-only for us; the owner applies store changes
Klaviyo is read and draft only; the owner switches flows on
assets: The existing abandoned-cart email in Klaviyo (not reviewed for a year)
Shopify analytics for the last 60 days
brief.technical_level: Not stated; the owner decides, so give ready changes to review with plain-language reasons
unknowns: Whether payment failures are part of the drop (no gateway data seen yet)
Which payment gateway and which payment methods (UPI, cards, COD, wallets) the store offers
Margin per order and the orders that actually completed (only analytics percentages given)
What the current abandoned-cart email says, when it sends and whether it is switched on
Checkout completion split by mobile and desktop, and by cart value
Brand voice and any brand guide

answers.question: Store, platform and market?
answers.answer: Clothing store on Shopify, selling in India

answers.question: Where are you now?
answers.answer: Add-to-cart rate about 9%; only 28% of checkouts started are completed (Shopify analytics, last 60 days); about 80% of traffic is mobile

answers.question: Limits?
answers.answer: Free shipping only above Rs 999 and it cannot be lowered; no margin cut

answers.question: Tools?
answers.answer: Klaviyo connected with read and draft access; Shopify MCP connected read-only; an abandoned-cart email exists but nobody has looked at it in a year

answers.question: Target and deadline?
answers.answer: Completed checkouts up to 40% by the end of January

answers.question: Data home and who decides?
answers.answer: Keep data in a CSV here; the owner decides

answers.question: Are payment failures part of it?

research.approach: Practitioners separate unavoidable abandonment (browsers, price checks) from fixable abandonment before changing anything. They measure the checkout funnel step by step and by device, check how the completion figure is defined, and read the payment gateway's failed-attempt report, because in India payment failure and missing payment methods (UPI intent, COD) are common and invisible in store analytics. They walk the real mobile checkout on a mid-range phone, then fix the largest cause first: surprise costs and shipping messaging, payment methods and flow, form length and forced accounts, speed. The abandoned-cart email is audited as its own system (trigger, timing, filters, copy) and judged by revenue per recipient against the platform benchmarks. Each change goes live as a registered test with a held-back group, and is read on enough checkouts to mean something.

sources.title: Baymard Institute: cart abandonment rate statistics
sources.note: Average documented abandonment about 70%. Reasons after 'just browsing': extra costs 40%, slow delivery 20%, distrust 19%, forced account 18%, long checkout 17%, site errors 17%. Says to separate unavoidable from fixable abandonment.

sources.title: Shopify Help Center: abandoned checkouts
sources.note: Accessed 2026-11-03. A checkout counts as abandoned only after the shopper gives an email and leaves for 10 minutes, so earlier leavers are invisible. The checkout Timeline shows payment attempts and messages. Recovery emails are not sent after a payment processing error. An emails report shows sessions, orders and sales from recovery emails.

sources.title: Razorpay: Shopify checkout issues and fixes in India
sources.note: Payment failures, UPI intent flow, COD handling, mobile tap targets and autofill, app scripts breaking checkout. Vendor article that sells payments products, so performance claims are unverified.

sources.title: Klaviyo Help Center: performance benchmarks for flows
sources.note: Abandoned cart flow benchmarks are revenue per recipient by revenue band and order value, shown as 25th and 75th percentiles and not guaranteed.

sources.title: Welcome, cart and browse email rollout planner

steps.name: Pin down what 'completed' means and the funnel steps
steps.why: A 28% figure only guides action when its definition and the step-by-step funnel by device are known.

steps.name: Pull the checkout funnel, abandoned checkouts and email flow results
steps.why: Raw exports by device, cart value and step show where people leave; abandoned-checkout timelines show payment attempts; the flow report shows what recovery brings back today.

steps.name: Check the completion figure against real orders
steps.why: Bots, definitions and double counting can move the figure before any fix does.

steps.name: Walk the real mobile checkout and the payment options
steps.why: Slow pages, long forms, forced accounts and missing UPI or COD show up on a real phone, not in a report.

steps.name: Audit the abandoned-cart flow
steps.why: A year-old flow may be off, late, or mis-triggered, and its results give a benchmark gap.

steps.name: Test the causes against the data and rank the fixes
steps.why: Cost, payment, mobile and email each need a different fix; the biggest measured cause goes first.

steps.name: Draft the email and checkout fixes
steps.why: Fix the flow (timing, two flows so nobody gets both, no discount) and the store settings the diagnosis supports.

steps.name: Apply as registered tests with a held-back group and read honestly
steps.why: A before-and-after in a sale month is not proof; a holdout and enough checkouts are.

pitfalls.text: Treating all abandonment as fixable: a large share is shoppers who were never going to buy, so a 40% target must be tested against the recoverable pool.
Judging the cart email by open rate instead of placed orders or revenue per recipient.
Missing payment failures because store analytics does not show them; they live in the gateway report.
Offering a discount to recover carts, which cuts margin and the owner has ruled it out.
Sending both a cart email and a checkout email to the same shopper.

plan.name: Lift checkout completion without cutting margin

capabilities.why: Pull checkout funnel, abandoned checkouts and orders.

capabilities.name: Read email flows and results (Klaviyo)

data.name: Checkout funnel by step, device and cart value
data.why: Shows which step loses people and whether mobile differs from desktop.

routes.how: Read with the Shopify MCP: last 60 days (and the 60 days before), daily, by device.
Shopify admin > Analytics > Reports > Conversion over time and checkout funnel; export CSV.

data.alternative: Without step data, only the headline 28% and order totals are usable; the leaking step stays unknown.

data.name: Abandoned checkouts
data.why: Shows cart value, items, payment attempts in the checkout timeline, and which were recoverable by email. Shopify counts a checkout as abandoned only after an email is given.

routes.how: Read abandoned checkouts with the Shopify MCP for the same 60 days.
Shopify admin > Orders > Abandoned checkouts; export CSV.

data.alternative: Without it, cart-value and shipping-threshold findings stay unknown.

data.name: Completed orders
data.why: Checks the completion figure against real orders and gives margin per order.

routes.how: Read orders for the same period with the Shopify MCP.

data.alternative: Without orders, the completion figure stays a report and the check is marked LIMITED.

data.name: Payment attempts and failures
data.why: The owner does not know whether payment failures are part of the problem; only the gateway shows it.

routes.how: Gateway dashboard > Payments > export for the last 60 days, by payment method.
Ask the owner which gateway and methods the store uses, and for the export.

data.alternative: Without it, the payment-failure hypothesis stays UNKNOWN and is not ranked.

data.name: Abandoned-cart flow setup and results
data.why: Shows when emails send, who is excluded and what the flow earns per recipient.

routes.how: Read the flow and its report for the last 60 days with the Klaviyo connection.
Klaviyo > Flows > the flow > Analytics; export.

data.alternative: Without it, the email fix is drafted from the checklist and the benchmark gap stays unknown.

stages.name: Pin down the problem
stages.goal: Turn the owner's words into a measured problem, a target, limits and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Gather the checkout data in one place
stages.goal: Pull the funnel by step and device, abandoned checkouts, orders, gateway attempts and the email flow results into one CSV set.

checks.name: Completed-order count in the dataset matches the Shopify orders export for the same dates within 1%
Covers the last 60 days and the 60 days before, so a trend is visible
Any export not provided (for example the gateway report) is listed as missing with what it would unlock

stages.name: Check the 28% figure can be trusted
stages.goal: Confirm how checkout completion is defined, strip bot or duplicate checkouts, and reconcile with real orders before anyone reasons from it.

checks.name: States whether completion is completed divided by checkouts started, and the same definition is used in both 60-day periods
Completed checkouts and orders agree within 5%, or the gap is explained
Ends with CHECKED, LIMITED or UNRELIABLE and what that means for the 40% target

stages.name: Walk the real mobile checkout
stages.goal: Step through the live checkout on a mid-range phone view to the payment step: shipping cost visibility, forced account, form fields, payment methods offered (UPI, cards, COD, wallets) and speed.

checks.name: Every checkout step is recorded with screenshots and the count of fields on each
Mobile load of the checkout pages is measured, and each page that takes over 2.5 s is flagged
Payment completion is marked not tested, because no real payment is made

stages.name: Audit the abandoned-cart flow
stages.goal: Read how the current abandoned-cart flow is set up: trigger, status, timing, filters, whether the cart and checkout flows overlap, and revenue per recipient against the Klaviyo benchmark.

checks.name: Records whether the flow is live, its trigger and the delay before the first email
Records whether any shopper can get both a cart email and a checkout email
Revenue per recipient is compared with the Klaviyo benchmark row for the store's order value, or marked unknown

stages.name: Find where the other 72% leave
stages.goal: Test the hypotheses against the funnel, abandoned checkouts, gateway and flow data. Separate shoppers who were never buying from the recoverable pool. Keep competing explanations.

checks.name: Every hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN, with the rows it rests on
A segment finding is made only with at least 100 checkouts started in the segment, otherwise marked low-confidence
Estimates how many extra completions the 40% target needs and whether the supported causes can plausibly deliver them
Each main finding names a competing explanation

stages.name: Rank what to change
stages.goal: Turn supported findings into ranked fix cards, each inside the limits (no discount, Rs 999 threshold unchanged).

checks.name: Every card cites the finding it rests on
Every card has expected effect in completion points, effort, confidence, risk to margin and how it will be measured
No card needs a discount, a price cut or a change to the Rs 999 threshold

stages.name: Owner chooses
stages.goal: The owner picks card IDs. Ask for the reason when they pass over a top card; record it.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over cards are in decisions.jsonl
A reason is recorded wherever a top card was passed over

stages.name: Draft the new cart and checkout emails
stages.goal: Draft two flows in Klaviyo as drafts: added to cart and checkout started, so nobody gets both, with timing, filters and copy in the store's voice and no discount.

checks.name: Rules stop anyone who ordered, and stop a cart email going to someone who has started checkout
No email offers a discount or price cut
Everything is saved as a Klaviyo draft, nothing is live
A random 10% holdout is specified so the flow can be compared with no email

stages.name: Prepare the checkout changes
stages.goal: Write exact steps for the chosen store changes (payment methods and UPI flow, shipping-cost message and cart nudge toward Rs 999, guest checkout, form fields, speed), each with how to confirm it worked.

checks.name: Only chosen changes are included
Each change says how to undo it
Each change says how to confirm it in Shopify or the gateway report

stages.name: Switch on the new email flows
stages.goal: Register the test, then the owner switches on each flow in Klaviyo after we show it. Read the live settings back.

checks.name: The test, holdout and start date are in experiments.jsonl before anything is switched on
Live trigger, delay, filters and holdout read back from Klaviyo match the approved drafts

stages.name: Apply the checkout changes
stages.goal: Register each change as a test, then the owner applies it in Shopify admin, one at a time, after we show it. Read back the result.

checks.name: Each change has its date and expected effect in experiments.jsonl before it is applied
Changes go live in separate steps, at least 7 days apart where traffic allows, so effects can be told apart
Each change is confirmed in Shopify after it is applied

stages.name: Read the results honestly
stages.goal: Read completion by device and by payment method every week against the 28% baseline and the guardrails; compare the flow with its holdout; flag any slip early.

checks.name: A verdict is given only with at least 250 checkout starts per compared group, otherwise INCONCLUSIVE
Add-to-cart rate, margin per order, returns and unsubscribes are each checked
Compared periods have the same length and the same definition of completion; any sale days are marked

stages.name: Keep what we learned
stages.goal: Close each experiment, save rules with their scope, and plan the next round.

checks.name: Every registered experiment is closed in experiments.jsonl with a verdict
Each rule says whether it holds for this job, this store or the playbook

hypotheses.statement: Payment failures or missing payment methods lose a large share of shoppers who reach the payment step.
hypotheses.test: Gateway success rate by method and device; payment-step drop-off in the funnel; methods offered versus UPI, cards, COD and wallets.
hypotheses.confirm_if: More than 10% of payment attempts fail, or mobile payment success is 5 points or more below desktop, or UPI or COD is not offered.
hypotheses.refute_if: Payment attempts succeed above 95% and the payment step loses under 5% of those who reach it.

hypotheses.statement: Shoppers leave when they see shipping cost on carts below Rs 999.
hypotheses.test: Completion rate and drop-off step for carts below Rs 999 versus Rs 999 and above; step at which shipping cost first appears.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Completion for carts below Rs 999 is 10 points or more lower than for carts above, with most leaving at the shipping step.

hypotheses.statement: The mobile checkout is much worse than desktop (forms, tap targets, speed).
hypotheses.test: Completion by device; field count and load time on the mobile walk-through.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Mobile completion is 8 points or more below desktop, or any checkout page loads in over 2.5 s on a mid-range phone.
hypotheses.refute_if: Mobile and desktop completion are within 3 points and pages load under 2.5 s.

hypotheses.statement: Forced account creation or a long form pushes people out before payment.
hypotheses.test: Walk-through: guest checkout available, field count; funnel drop at the contact-information step.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Guest checkout is off, or the contact step loses more than 25% of those who reach it.
hypotheses.refute_if: Guest checkout is on and the contact step loses under 10%.

hypotheses.statement: The abandoned-cart email is late, off or mis-triggered, so recoverable shoppers are lost.
hypotheses.test: Flow status, trigger, delay and filters; revenue per recipient against the Klaviyo benchmark row; share of abandoned checkouts with a captured email.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The flow is off, the first email goes after more than 2 hours, or revenue per recipient is below the benchmark's 25th percentile.
hypotheses.refute_if: The flow is live, sends within 2 hours and earns at or above the benchmark's 75th percentile.

hypotheses.statement: Much of the 72% were never going to buy, so 40% is hard to reach by fixes alone.
hypotheses.test: Share of started checkouts that never became an abandoned checkout (no email given, so invisible in the abandoned list), and the extra completions needed for 40%.
hypotheses.confirm_if: More than half of checkouts started never give an email address.
hypotheses.refute_if: Most abandoned checkouts reach the shipping or payment step.

hypotheses.statement: The 28% figure is distorted by bots, duplicates or a different definition from the one assumed.
hypotheses.test: Reconcile completed checkouts to orders; check the definition and bot filtering.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Completed checkouts and orders differ by more than 5%, or the definition changed between periods.
hypotheses.refute_if: They agree within 5% and the definition is stable.

measurement.window: At least 4 weeks after the last change, and 2 weeks per email flow test; compare against the 60 days before and a 10% holdout for email.
measurement.min_volume: At least 250 checkout starts per compared group to see a 12-point change; below that the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE.
measurement.stop_rule: Stop and undo a change at once if margin per order falls, add-to-cart rate drops 1 point or more, or payment failures rise; otherwise run the full window.
